abstract="Vaccines are widely used in both research and clinical settings. To facilitate FAIR data practices, we urgently need to standardize vaccine representation, integrate information across diverse vaccine types, and support computer-assisted reasoning. Accordingly, we have since 2007 developed the community-based Vaccine Ontology (VO), which aligns with the Basic Formal Ontology and adheres to OBO Foundry principles. VO ontologically models vaccines, vaccine components, vaccine immune responses, vaccine investigation studies and other vaccine-related topics. VO represents more than 10,000 vaccines targeting 289 infectious pathogens and cancers in humans and over 30 nonhuman animal species. VO provides mappings to external resources such as RxNorm, CVX, FDA, and USDA. VO facilitates vaccine standardization in resources such as the VIOLIN vaccine database, ImmPort, and the Vaccine Adjuvant Compendium (VAC). VO enables semantic queries on vaccine data. It has been shown to enhance the analysis of experimental and clinical vaccine datasets, as well as vaccine-related literature mining. Overall, VO standardizes vaccine modeling and representation and greatly supports vaccine AI research in the Semantic Web era.",

conditionsOfAccess: The most recent release version of the VO document (OWL DL format) is always available here for download:
dct:provenance: Metadata evidence: live Step 7 comparison confirmed that the exact name occurs on the VO-specific VIOLIN homepage. The description is an exact contiguous paragraph from that homepage, replacing the different description previously taken from the ontology annotation. version, release date, creators, and CC BY 4.0 license are declared in the configured VO OWL file and authoritative registries. The license URL is the canonical URL shown on the live Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International deed, and OBO Foundry identifies VO's license as CC BY 4.0. conditionsOfAccess is an exact sentence from the live authoritative VO Download page. citeAs is the exact BibTeX returned by the live Scientific Data citation-download endpoint linked from the article's Cite this article section; it contains the complete final author list, title, journal, date, volume, issue, article number, DOI, and URL rather than the superseded preprint citation. No source explicitly assigns a publisher role, so publisher is omitted rather than inferred from a hosting organization. Distribution: all 256 successful manifest items marked as distribution candidates are represented as distinct cr:FileObject entries; no manifest distribution candidate was excluded. Each contentUrl is the final direct URL observed during the crawl with HTTP 200, and contentSize and sha256 are computed from the downloaded bytes. Mutable current assets and immutable tagged releases are retained separately even when byte-identical because they are distinct public assets. HTML evidence pages are excluded from distribution. Schema derivation: 32 record sets and 330 fields were generated from exact in-band header tokens; 6 SSSOM tables had leading comment/preamble metadata and 20 ROBOT CSV templates had a directive/schema row. Datatype inference used at most five data records per table. 8 repeated header occurrences were not modeled because a name-only source.extract.column selector cannot distinguish any occurrence; the observed names were realized in (src/templates/other.csv) and comment (src/templates/protein.csv, vaccine.csv, and vaccine_component.csv). No header token was normalized. No record sets were fabricated for OWL/RDF/XML, SPARQL query text, office documents, spreadsheets, or other non-tabular assets because Croissant extraction cannot honestly express their graph, query, or worksheet semantics. The BioPortal CSV export was delivered as gzip and remains a distribution object but has no record set because a decompression/extraction mapping is not declared by the source. Crawl limitations: hundreds of duplicate historical BioPortal mirror submissions and mutable non-release development branches were not downloaded; all 22 formal upstream tags and the recursively linked 2017 SourceForge tree were downloaded. The obsolete VIOLIN page's src/VO_merged.owl URL returned 404; current vo.owl is established by the configured source and OBO PURL configuration. Authentication-gated assets were excluded, and byte-identical mirror aliases were not redundantly saved unless they represented a distinct format or historical release. Step 8 final repair audit: all five required top-level fields were non-empty; all 256 distribution contentUrl values were unique and returned HTTP 200 with no retry, authentication response, 404 removal, or dependent-reference repair. Inspection of 283 downloaded files found no true release archive; 30 ZIP-signature files were semantic office containers and one gzip was a single compressed CSV stream, so no inner archive FileObjects or RecordSets were added. All 256 FileObjects had encodingFormat values consistent with their local signatures and contents. All 334 initially represented Fields resolved to exactly one source FileObject and an exact observed column token; four Fields using duplicate-name selectors were removed because the selector could not distinguish either occurrence, leaving 330 verified Fields. No source reference or selector could be corrected more truthfully. Relaxed geographic matching found no location-oriented source columns. The site.csv table was not given a GeoCoordinates parent because generic LABEL and Parent columns mix countries, routes, and other site classes and do not form a coherent row-level location.
description: To ensure consistent representation of vaccine knowledge and to support automated reasoning, a community-based effort to develop the Vaccine Ontology (VO) has been initiated. This international collaborative VO development effort has been joined by many institutes and disciplines around the world. The Vaccine Ontology is also being used in a variety of applications by many user groups in academia and industry.
